sections.heading: 1. Try this mix
lines: ① Pilates 1–2 times a week for control.
② Weights once a week for heavier load.
③ Make the last few reps genuinely hard.
④ Add single-leg and standing exercises.

slides.heading: Worth an assessment first if

caption:
Momo has done reformer twice a week for a year and is wondering if she still needs the gym.

Pilates does build strength, especially around the trunk, hips and shoulders. But springs only go so heavy and a lot of it happens lying down, so whether it's enough depends on your goal. For moving well and managing a back niggle, it may be plenty. For heavier lifting or bone health, adding a weights session can help.

Ask your instructor to keep progressing springs, reps and standing work. Our Pilates team at Hybrid Physio can help you plan the mix. Book online via the link in bio.
